questions.q: Without partitioning, what does Athena actually do when a query filters for a single day (e.g. WHERE dt = '2026-08-15')?
options: It still scans every file in the table, applying the date filter only after reading all the data
It automatically skips every file that doesn't match the date, with no setup required
It refuses to run the query until the table is partitioned
It only scans the single matching file, because CSV files are inherently date-aware
questions.explain: Without partition information, the WHERE clause is just a row filter applied after scanning everything — Athena has no way to know in advance which files could match.

questions.q: What is a "partition column" like `dt` in this lesson's example?
options: A column derived from the S3 folder path (dt=2026-08-15/), not stored as data inside the CSV files
A column that must be manually typed into every row of every CSV file
A special Athena-only data type unrelated to S3 folder structure
A column that only exists in Redshift, never in Athena
questions.explain: Partition columns come from the folder structure itself — the crawler infers dt from the dt= prefix naming convention, not from file contents.

questions.q: After physically reorganizing the S3 files into dt= partitions, what has to happen before Athena can use them?
options: The Glue Crawler needs to be re-run so the Catalog registers the new partitions
Nothing — Athena automatically detects any S3 folder structure change instantly
The orders_raw table must be deleted and manually recreated from scratch
The raw CSV files must be converted to JSON first
questions.explain: Re-running the same crawler discovers the new dt= folders and registers dt as a partition column on the existing table.

options: Athena skipping entire partitions it knows can't match a query's filter, without scanning any bytes from them
Deleting old partitions automatically after 90 days
A Glue ETL step that removes duplicate rows from a partitioned table
Compressing files within a partition to save storage space
questions.explain: Partition pruning is the mechanism that lets Athena skip whole folders based on Catalog metadata, rather than opening every file to check.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say partitioning makes almost no visible difference at this project's current scale, but matters a great deal later?
options: Athena bills per terabyte scanned, and the pruning ratio holds at any scale — it just costs real money and real wait time only once the dataset grows large
Partitioning only works correctly on datasets larger than 1 TB
Small datasets are exempt from Athena's per-query billing model entirely
Glue Crawlers cannot create partitions on tables under a certain row count
questions.explain: The underlying pruning benefit is proportionally identical at any scale — it's just invisible in dollars and seconds until the dataset is large enough for the difference to show up.
